questions.question: What does a strong PIQA score support most directly?
options: Performance on a defined set of two-choice physical-affordance questions under the recorded protocol
General common sense across every culture and product workflow
Safe execution of physical instructions in the real world
Reliable social and emotional inference
questions.explanation: PIQA is a narrow physical common-sense signal. Product safety, open-ended generation, cultures, and other common-sense dimensions need separate evidence.

questions.question: What is the core invariant when choosing a world knowledge benchmark?
options: Match the benchmark's evidence contract to the product claim
Always choose the dataset with the most questions
Blend every score into one world-knowledge percentage
Require the same answer length for every benchmark
questions.explanation: Closed-book recall, open-domain retrieval, and supplied-passage reading support different claims and expose different failure paths.

questions.question: Which condition is required before two MATH accuracy numbers are directly comparable?
options: They use the same task revision, prompt, decoding budget, answer verifier, and aggregation contract
They were published in the same calendar year
They both include a generated explanation
They use models with the same parameter count
questions.explanation: The measurement contract determines what the score means. Model size, publication date, or explanation length does not make different harnesses comparable.

questions.question: For a task with n generated candidates and c passing candidates, what does pass@k estimate?
options: The probability that at least one of k sampled candidates passes the declared tests
The percentage of source lines that parse successfully
The probability that the first candidate is safe to deploy
The number of hidden tests in the benchmark
questions.explanation: pass@k measures whether a set of k candidates contains a passing solution under the declared test contract. It is not a safety or maintainability score.

questions.question: Which condition is required before two MMLU scores can be compared defensibly?
options: The dataset, prompt, demonstrations, answer ordering, decoding, and extractor are held constant or their changes are explicitly studied
Both models produce fluent explanations
Both scores are above 80%
The newer model has more parameters
questions.explanation: A score is tied to its protocol. Uncontrolled prompt, data, inference, or extraction changes can create apparent model differences.

questions.question: What does an arena preference score establish most directly?
options: How often sampled voters preferred one model over its opponents under the evaluated conditions
That the highest-rated model is factually correct on every prompt
That the leading model satisfies every product safety policy
The absolute quality of a model independently of its opponents
questions.explanation: Arena evidence is relative and conditional on the opponents, prompts, voters, interface, and time window. It does not establish absolute correctness or safety.
